quizzes.stem: A team needs an agent to run a task for several hours, survive restarts of its own service, and be resumed the next day, and it does not want to build a sandbox. Which option fits?

options.a: The Client SDK's tool runner, which hosts the sandbox for the loop
options.b: The Messages API alone, which stores the conversation for each request
options.c: The Claude Code CLI, started again by hand each morning
options.d: The hosted harness, which stores sessions on Anthropic's side

explanation.d: The overview table gives "Long-running tasks and asynchronous work" as the best fit, and says sessions "resume cleanly after pauses" with history and outputs stored server-side, so your service holds only an ID.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the Messages API is "Direct model prompting access", for "Custom agent loops and fine-grained control", and you keep the history yourself.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the CLI is something you drive yourself: "You use the CLI by hand."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says the tool runner "drives the same kind of loop inside your process and hosts nothing", while the sandbox belongs to the hosted product.

quizzes.stem: A session is created with a tools override that names one tool, while the saved agent lists eight. What does the session have?

options.a: Only that lone entry, with nothing else carried over
options.b: The entry together with the agent's eight, merged into one list
options.c: The agent's eight, which an override cannot remove
options.d: None, until the agent is updated to a new version

explanation.a: The page says "Overrides never merge with the agent's configuration, so a `tools` override must list every tool the session should have."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Overrides never merge with the agent's configuration", so nothing is added to the entry.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "overrides replace and never merge", so the agent's own list is not kept beside the entry.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "They apply to that one session, and the agent resource and its version are untouched.", so nothing waits for a new agent version.

quizzes.stem: A compliance team requires Zero Data Retention for every Claude workload. What follows for Managed Agents?

options.a: It qualifies once the sandbox runs on the team's own network
options.b: It qualifies, since ZDR covers every endpoint of the API
options.c: It is ineligible today, since sessions store history server-side
options.d: It qualifies once the sessions have been deleted afterwards

explanation.c: The overview says sessions "store conversation history, sandbox state, and outputs server-side", so they are held on Anthropic's side.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Self-hosted sandboxes keep the orchestration on Anthropic's side but move tool execution into infrastructure you control", so the session data still sits with Anthropic.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the overview says "Managed Agents is not currently eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) coverage", not that it is covered.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "You can delete sessions and files through the API, but the data exists on Anthropic's side first", so deletion does not make it qualify.

quizzes.stem: A team creates an environment with `packages` and `limited` networking and lists the registries in `allowed_hosts`, but sets nothing else. What happens?

options.a: The packages install, since the hosts are on the allowed list
options.b: The request is rejected until the registry flag is true
options.c: The environment is created with unrestricted networking instead
options.d: The packages install after a warning that the agent can ignore

explanation.b: The page says "If the environment uses `limited` networking, also set `networking.allow_package_managers` to `true`; otherwise the request is rejected with a 400 error."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page requires "also set `networking.allow_package_managers` to `true`", and listing hosts alone does not open the registries.
explanation.c: Ruled out because only "a create request that omits it gets `unrestricted`", and here the field is set to `limited`.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page names a rejection and not a warning: "otherwise the request is rejected with a 400 error."

quizzes.stem: A cloud agent reads untrusted pages, keeps the default toolset policy and has `limited` networking with a few allowed hosts. Which change limits what a prompt injection can send out through those hosts?

options.a: Replace the allowed hosts with wildcard patterns
options.b: Switch the toolset to custom tools so that no policy applies
options.c: Restrict the web tools with an allowed domains list
options.d: Make bash wait for approval before each command

explanation.d: The page advises to "set the `bash` tool's policy to `always_ask` or `auto`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The sandbox can send any request to an allowed host", so wider host patterns open more places to send to.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Custom tools are executed by your application and controlled by you", so they would move the risk into your code and not remove it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools "run on Anthropic's servers, so `networking` does not govern them", and a domain list on them leaves the sandbox's own route open.

quizzes.stem: A session created with a budget of `"500"` goes idle with a list cost of 503 cents. How should the team read this?

options.a: As intended, with the running request allowed to finish
options.b: As a billing error that the platform should refund
options.c: As a failed check that ran in the middle of a request
options.d: As a crash that ended the session for good

explanation.a: The page says "The request in flight when the cap is crossed still finishes", so a paused session can read a fraction past the cap.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "it bounds new work and not the exact total", so a figure past the cap is not an error.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The cap is checked between requests, so it bounds new work", and not in the middle of a request.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A session at its cap does not die." Its history and sandbox are kept.

quizzes.stem: A hospital group must keep patient files inside its own network but wants Anthropic to run the agent loop. Which setup fits?

options.a: A cloud sandbox with `limited` networking and a few allowed hosts
options.b: A self-hosted sandbox whose tools execute on local machines
options.c: The Messages API with the files pasted into each prompt
options.d: The Agent SDK running in the group's own process

explanation.b: The page says "Self-hosted sandboxes keep the orchestration on Anthropic's side but move tool execution into infrastructure you control", and the group still owns the image and the egress rules.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "By default tools run in Anthropic's sandboxes.", so the files would be processed on Anthropic's side.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "You write the loop on the Messages API.", and the group wants Anthropic to run the loop.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "You embed Claude Code's loop with the Agent SDK, in a process you operate.", so the group, not Anthropic, would run it.

quizzes.stem: A developer migrates an Agent SDK service whose `can_use_tool` callback approved reads and refused pushes. What replaces that callback in Managed Agents?

options.a: A per-tool permission policy, with confirmations sent as events
options.b: The `ClaudeAgentOptions` object, created again for every run
options.c: The environment's `networking` field, which approves each command
options.d: A model override on the session that removes the tool

explanation.a: The first page says `permission_mode` and `can_use_tool` "become a per-tool permission policy", and a paused call is answered with a `user.tool_confirmation` event.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the migration "becomes an agent created once" from that object.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `networking` controls the sandbox's outbound traffic, and "so `networking` does not govern them" for the search and fetch tools.
explanation.d: Ruled out because an override "must list every tool the session should have", and removing a tool is not an approval step.

quizzes.stem: A product relays customers' messages to an agent as `user.message` events and sets the toolset to `auto`. What is the risk?

options.a: Their text counts as the operator's own intent when a call is judged
options.b: The server ignores `user.message` events once a policy is set
options.c: Every call pauses until a person has confirmed it
options.d: A denied call can be overridden by the client with a confirmation

explanation.a: The page says "If you relay untrusted end-user input in `user.message` events, the server reads that input as your intent too."
explanation.b: Ruled out because what you post in `user.message` events "counts as your intent", so the server reads it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "`auto` is not a human checkpoint", and a safe call "runs before anyone sees it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a denied call is final: "your client cannot override the denial."

quizzes.stem: A finance team wants to know what one long session's reported cost contains. Which items make up that total?

options.a: Model tokens, event-history storage and disk space
options.b: Model tokens alone, with sandbox time left free
options.c: Model tokens, web searches and running time
options.d: Model tokens and web searches, with running time billed apart

explanation.c: The page says the total is "model tokens at each model's list price, web searches at $10 per 1,000", and "Session running time, at $0.08 per hour".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The documentation lists these three items and no other.", and storage and disk are not among them.
explanation.b: Ruled out because running time is priced: "Session running time, at $0.08 per hour".
explanation.d: Ruled out because running time is one of the three items of "the total is its list cost", not a separate bill.
